source.title: On the Tunability of Optimizers in Deep Learning
source.authors: Prabhu Teja Sivaprasad; Florian Mai; Thijs Vogels; Martin Jaggi; François Fleuret

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix text supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers using held-out performance across tuning budgets; its tuning protocol differs from the optimizer comparisons summarized in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test-performance comparisons for optimizers and tuning budgets. Cited results from Wilson et al. and other prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with SGD variants using held-out performance under controlled random-search budgets. These results test V4 with a different tuning protocol. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors advocate including tuning cost in optimizer benchmarks and find Adam-LR the most reliable practical choice under their calibrated cross-task random-search protocol, especially at low budgets. SGD wins in some settings, while tuning all Adam parameters can improve selected high-budget outcomes with greater variability.
record.recipe_differences: Benchmarks optimizer hyperparameter search on nine tasks with calibrated cross-task priors and random search; reports held-out performance at varying tuning budgets rather than comparing fixed optimizer recipes alone.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance changes with tuning budget, dataset/task, and the number of optimizer hyperparameters tuned; the paper also reports differences when using computation time rather than trial count as the budget unit, while stating the overall pattern remains similar.

fits_no_version.finding: Tuning additional Adam or SGD hyperparameters can reduce low-budget performance and improve selected higher-budget outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The value of tuning additional optimizer hyperparameters depends on task, search budget, and variability across searches.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizer CPE reconstruction losses differ on MNIST-VAE and FMNIST-VAE, and optimization losses differ on an artificial quadratic problem.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer performance under limited hyperparameter search varies across reconstruction and artificial optimization tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam has broad regions of good performance as learning rate varies on several tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width of a favorable hyperparameter region predicts ease of random-search tuning; this is distinct from weight-perturbation sharpness predicting generalization gaps.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The authors note that the study does not test Bayesian HPO, assumes independent hyperparameter priors, and does not model complex relationships between hyperparameters in its main protocol. The aggregate performance summaries do not provide uncertainty in the cited comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Rows R9-R17 extract the Adam-LR CPE values across all nine task columns. Other optimizer values in Table 6 were not separately recorded; the table and surrounding text provide the key comparisons, and the 60-row limit was not reached.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Whether held-out differences coexist with equal or better training performance; decoupled weight decay for Adam; switching Adam to SGD; the word-level language-model exception; and whether broader tuning removes an Adam–SGD gap under the original studies' protocols. IMDb is sentiment classification. The tested search distributions are calibrated across tasks, with validation-based stopping, rather than reproducing Wilson et al.'s tuning protocol.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and generalization gaps. The paper's hyperparameter-surface widths are a different construct.
Removing memorized examples and comparing retrained test accuracy with random removal.

missing.what: Budget-specific optimizer-family comparisons: SGD variants become better choices on CIFAR-100 and Char-RNN at later HPO stages. Record the probability-of-best measure separately from CPE; the supplied text does not identify numerical probabilities or the winning variants.
missing.locator: Appendix C, Figure 6 and accompanying text

missing.what: CIFAR-10 learning-rate-surface comparison: similarly broad favorable learning-rate regions give comparable low-budget performance, while SGD-MC WC's higher maximum gives better high-budget performance.
missing.locator: Appendix G, Figure 8 and accompanying text

missing.what: The aggregate Adam-LR advantage persists when HPO budget is measured in computation rather than trial count. Record this as a robustness result and retain the mixed-task scope of the aggregate.

Accounting for learning-rate/momentum dependence improves SGD's low-budget performance, particularly on classification tasks, but the resulting SGD variant remains below Adam-LR in the cross-task aggregate at all budgets.

record.verdict_notes: Only V4 is tested. The record's low-budget supports label has the direction backward: Adam-LR outperforming SGD challenges the adaptive disadvantage in those settings. CPE is a weighted summary of held-out performance across search budgets, not a single-budget result. Aggregate results mix classification, language, reconstruction, and artificial optimization tasks, so per-task comparisons provide the clearest evidence for V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond interpolation and test error.

Broader per-dataset hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and the specific optimizer comparisons in Wilson et al. are not tested. The paper does include an IMDb word-level LSTM task.

rows.subject: Adam-LR
rows.operation_detail: Trained with only the learning rate tuned; compared with SGD variants across aggregate tasks and tuning budgets.
rows.baseline: Adam-LR reference; SGD variants perform 20% worse early in HPO and the gap narrows to 10% as budgets increase.
rows.value: Adam-LR performs very close to the best optimizer for all budgets.
rows.note: The stated percentages describe the SGD variants' relative performance gap to Adam-LR, not a per-dataset value.
rows.check: Adam-LR outperforming SGD reverses the adaptive-method disadvantage; it does not support that disadvantage. The reported 20% and 10% gaps are aggregate relative-performance differences across nine heterogeneous tasks, including tasks outside V4, not accuracy-point differences on image or language benchmarks.
